arms.predicted: BnB with degeneracy ordering, BBMC-style bitset coloring bound, and greedy restarts will achieve score >= 95, substantially outperforming greedy-only.
arms.observed: Scores: 90, 100, 100 (mean 96.7). The 90 outlier is from system-load-induced timeout on one test case; 100 achieved in 2 of 3 runs. Best score: 100.
arms.diagnostic_note: The BBMC-style coloring (bitset-based independent set extraction) was critical for speed. Earlier implementations using pairwise O(n^2) coloring scored only 60-70 due to timing out on dense graphs.

arms.predicted: Greedy-only (no BnB) will score substantially lower than h-main, likely below 85.
arms.observed: Scores: 92.158, 92.158, 92.158 (perfectly consistent). Higher than predicted 85 threshold but consistently lower than h-main's best (100) and mean (96.7).
arms.diagnostic_note: Greedy with 5000 random restarts is stronger than expected (92 vs predicted <85). The gap to BnB (92 vs 100) still confirms BnB's value but greedy alone captures ~92% of optimal. The test graphs may have structure favoring greedy (e.g., max clique reachable from high-degree vertices).

discrepancy_analysis: h-main CONFIRMED: BnB achieves score 100 (>= 95 threshold). h-control-negative PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED: greedy scored 92.158, higher than the predicted <85 but still meaningfully lower than BnB (100). The directional claim (BnB > greedy) holds consistently. The magnitude prediction for greedy was off — 5000 random restarts with bitset-accelerated clique checks are stronger than anticipated.
